# Organs in the Nine Abdominal Regions — Printed page 60

**Source:** User-supplied photograph, study guide p. 60, “Organs in the Nine Abdominal Regions.” The source cites Berman, Snyder, and Frandsen (2016), p. 598; the complete book title/edition is not visible in the photo.

## Core idea
The nine-region scheme divides the abdomen into three rows and three columns. Right and left are named from the **patient’s perspective**, not the observer’s.

## Source table transcription

| Upper row | Structures listed on p. 60 |
|---|---|
| **Right hypochondriac** | Right lobe of liver; gallbladder; part of duodenum; hepatic flexure of colon; upper half of right kidney; suprarenal gland. |
| **Epigastric** | Aorta; pyloric end of stomach; part of duodenum; pancreas; part of liver. |
| **Left hypochondriac** | Stomach; spleen; tail of pancreas; splenic flexure of colon; upper half of left kidney; suprarenal gland. |

| Middle row | Structures listed on p. 60 |
|---|---|
| **Right lumbar** | Ascending colon; lower half of right kidney; part of duodenum and jejunum. |
| **Umbilical** | Omentum; mesentery; lower part of duodenum; part of jejunum and ileum. |
| **Left lumbar** | Descending colon; lower half of left kidney; part of jejunum and ileum. |

| Lower row | Structures listed on p. 60 |
|---|---|
| **Right inguinal** | Cecum; appendix; McBurney’s point; lower end of ileum; right ureter; right spermatic cord; right ovary. |
| **Hypogastric (pubic)** | Ileum; bladder; uterus. |
| **Left inguinal** | Sigmoid colon; left ureter; left spermatic cord; left ovary. |

## Layout map

| Patient’s right | Center | Patient’s left |
|---|---|---|
| Right hypochondriac | Epigastric | Left hypochondriac |
| Right lumbar | Umbilical | Left lumbar |
| Right inguinal | Hypogastric / pubic | Left inguinal |

## Memory anchors
- **Hypochondriac:** upper lateral regions under the ribs.
- **Epigastric:** upper middle region.
- **Umbilical:** center around the navel.
- **Lumbar:** middle lateral/flank regions.
- **Hypogastric/pubic:** lower middle region.
- **Inguinal/iliac:** lower lateral regions near the groin/hip.

## Added anatomical explanation
- The aorta and other organs may extend across more than one region; these are surface-location guides, not rigid borders.
- Kidneys and suprarenal (adrenal) glands are retroperitoneal; their portions can project into different regions.
- Ovaries and uterus are relevant to the lower abdominopelvic regions; their position changes with age, pregnancy, and bladder filling. Spermatic cords and ovaries/uterus are sex-specific structures shown together in the source's educational table.
- **McBurney’s point is a surface landmark, not an organ.** It is commonly described near the junction of the lateral and middle thirds of a line from the right anterior superior iliac spine toward the umbilicus.
- Pain in a region does not establish which organ is responsible; interpretation requires clinical history, examination, and often tests.

## Nine regions versus four quadrants
The nine-region scheme is more detailed. The four-quadrant scheme uses vertical and horizontal lines crossing near the umbilicus: right upper (RUQ), left upper (LUQ), right lower (RLQ), and left lower (LLQ). Do not mix the systems in an exam answer.

## Retrieval check
1. Where does the source list the gallbladder? **Right hypochondriac.**
2. Where is the pancreas listed? **Epigastric; its tail is also listed in the left hypochondriac region.**
3. Which region lists the cecum and appendix? **Right inguinal.**
4. Where are bladder and uterus listed? **Hypogastric/pubic.**
5. Which colon portions anchor the right and left lumbar regions? **Ascending colon on the right; descending colon on the left.**
6. Whose right/left determines region names? **The patient’s.**
